cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's audit machine check HANGS General Contracting's equipment and leases.
The equipment list rolls forward, with one odd entry.
It checks every purchase against its invoice. A $41,250 repair was booked as equipment, and one buy had no approval. A crane sold in March is still on the books.
Depreciation spreads an asset's cost over its working life. One excavator's life is half the policy's.
Lease accounting puts long rentals on the balance sheet, as a right-of-use asset and a debt. Two leases are missing.
Last, it weighs the findings against materiality, the size of mistake that matters, and writes the workpapers for the CPA.

All done. In profit, the mistakes nearly cancel out. But over $2.1 million of lease debt is missing from the balance sheet, and the sold crane is still on the books. Ten items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
